findings.title: Archival overflow regression passes while a closed latest period becomes falsely open
findings.reason: Green individual baseline and green semantic mutant; assert-one-test confirmed one executed case in each. Assert the latest returned period and its recorded reactivation, or the complete expected paired cohort, so dropping the newest event is detected. FIX VERIFIED IN ROUND TWO: the identical slice(1, ARCHIVAL_EVENT_LIMIT + 1) mutant now fails the strengthened final-period archivedAt/reactivatedAt assertion after a passing individual baseline. No production correction was necessary; the test now detects the demonstrated defect.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: The test seeds i=0..201, with an archive at every even i and a reactivation at every odd i. The descending 201-event SQL read returns i=201..1. Correct slice(0, 200), reversed, retains i=2..201 and returns 100 closed periods. Mutant slice(1, 201), reversed, retains i=1..200: pairArchivedPeriods ignores the leading reactivation at i=1 and emits 99 closed periods plus a falsely open final period at i=200. Both results have 100 periods and the same earliest archive at i=2, which are the only period facets asserted. The latest reactivation at i=201 is lost on the executed branch and the returned last reactivatedAt changes from its recorded date to null. This changes owner-visible history and is neither equivalent nor an unexecuted branch.

findings.title: Coverage omission test pins an incidental total paragraph count
findings.reason: The changed .rst-note count changes from 1 to exactly 2 solely because a legitimate historical disclosure was added. An additional valid disclosure would fail the test even when coverage omission and absence of blank notes remain correct. Assert the absent coverage sentence and present required disclosures, then use a non-vacuous per-note trimmed-text check to reject blank rendered notes without pinning the total. FIX VERIFIED IN ROUND TWO: the exact count was removed, positive disclosure assertions remain, and non-vacuous trimmed note checks reject both an empty and a whitespace-only coverage note in separate journaled mutations.
